_comment: Char ceilings for the always-loaded canon and its companions. A ceiling is a MAX: shrinking always passes. Raising one needs --update in its own justified commit, with a reason. See scripts/check_claudemd_budget.py. CLAUDE.md is loaded into EVERY session, so its size is a standing tax on all work; it was 349,512 chars before the v1.130.0 canon/changelog split and is budgeted at 82,000 to leave real working room without letting the changelog creep back in. The archive is budgeted generously because it is a grep target that is never auto-loaded - it is listed only so that 'shrink CLAUDE.md' cannot be satisfied by moving weight somewhere nobody is watching. ARCHIVE CEILING RAISED 420,000 -> 430,000 (v1.145.14). Three consecutive commits (v1.145.10, v1.145.13, v1.146.0) each had to compress genuine post-mortem narrative to fit, and v1.145.13 evicted part of the entry it superseded and recorded that 'shaving is spent'. Compressing the record to satisfy a cap degrades the exact thing the cap exists to protect. The reason for capping the archive is displacement - so that 'shrink CLAUDE.md' cannot be satisfied by moving canon somewhere nobody watches - and that reason is unaffected here: the archive is a grep target, never auto-loaded, so its size is not a per-session tax. CLAUDE.md's own 82,000 is untouched and is the ceiling that actually matters. Raised by 10,000 (2.4%), not opened up, so the next raise is still a deliberate act. RAISED AGAIN AT v1.147.1, both files, for two DIFFERENT reasons - measured, not estimated. docs/Neural.md: origin/dev stood at 39,997 of 40,000 - THREE chars of headroom - and v1.147.0's pane-pager entry took it to 40,830 before the MC work touched it at all. A behaviour doc that is actively maintained cannot live on 3 chars; the next writer's only options were to compress someone else's paragraph or skip documenting their change, and the second is what actually happens. Raised to 43,000 (+7.5%). docs/Changelog-Archive.md: the v1.145.14 raise to 430,000 left 919 chars by the time v1.148.0's post-mortem was written - one entry of headroom, i.e. a ceiling-raise commit per entry, which turns a growth SIGNAL into a per-entry tax and pressures writers to under-document exactly the near-misses worth recording. Raised to 445,000 (+3.5%). Neither is opened up: both remain deliberate acts, and CLAUDE.md's 82,000 - the ceiling that is a per-session tax and the only one that truly matters - is untouched at 70,657. RAISED AGAIN AT v1.149.2, archive only, and this time the previous raise's own stated reason is the evidence. v1.147.1 raised the archive to 445,000 BECAUSE 919 chars of headroom is 'one entry of headroom, i.e. a ceiling-raise commit per entry'. Measured two versions later, at origin/dev c4f2226d6+2: 444,403 of 445,000, i.e. 597 spare - LESS headroom than the condition that triggered the raise, reached in two commits. A +2.4% and a +3.5% step have now each been consumed within three commits, so the step size, not the ceiling, is what is wrong: raised to 460,000 (+3.4%), which is ~3 entries at the observed ~5kB median rather than ~0.1. Still a deliberate act, still not opened up, and the displacement reason is still unaffected (the archive is a grep target, never auto-loaded, so its size is not a per-session tax). CLAUDE.md's own 82,000 - the only ceiling that IS a per-session tax - is untouched at 70,657. NOT RAISED, and flagged instead: docs/Neural.md stands at 42,913 of 43,000, i.e. 87 chars, which is the same trap v1.147.1 described for that file ('a behaviour doc that is actively maintained cannot live on 3 chars'). It is left alone here only because this commit does not touch it; the next writer who does will have to raise it first. RAISED AT v1.152.0, BOTH files, and for docs/Neural.md the previous note is the instruction: v1.149.2 measured it at 42,913 of 43,000 (87 chars) and wrote 'it is left alone here only because this commit does not touch it; the next writer who does will have to raise it first'. This is that commit — the concepts payload is a new thing the app fetches, so the payload table in the behaviour doc is exactly where it belongs, and origin/dev had already grown the file to 43,350 on its own. Raised 43,000 -> 45,000 (+4.7%), which is ~4 payload-table-sized edits rather than one. docs/Changelog-Archive.md: origin/dev stands at 458,507 of 460,000, i.e. 1,493 spare — under a third of one entry at the observed ~5kB median, and the v1.149.2 raise that set 460,000 was itself justified by 597 spare being too little. That raise targeted '~3 entries' and lasted three commits, so the step is still short: raised 460,000 -> 480,000 (+4.3%), leaving ~18,600 after this entry, i.e. 3-4 entries. Both remain deliberate acts. CLAUDE.md's own 82,000 — the only ceiling that is a per-session tax — is untouched and this commit does not add to it beyond one payload clause (70,813). RAISED AT v1.155.3, ARCHIVE ONLY, and the arithmetic is the whole argument: origin/dev arrived at 479,847 of 480,000 - 153 chars, i.e. 3% of one entry at the observed ~5kB median - so the file was already in the state every previous note here calls the trap, and the next post-mortem of ANY size would have had to raise it. That is the fourth consecutive raise consumed within a handful of commits (430,000 -> 445,000 -> 460,000 -> 480,000), and each note said the step, not the ceiling, was what was wrong. Raised 480,000 -> 510,000 (+6.25%), which leaves ~19,000 after this entry: 3-4 entries at the median rather than 0.03. docs/Neural.md is NOT raised - this change's paragraph was trimmed to fit the 857 chars origin/dev left, deliberately, because that file is the one a session actually reads. CLAUDE.md's 82,000 - the only ceiling that is a per-session tax - is untouched at 73,763. RAISED AT v1.163.0, docs/Neural.md only, and this is the THIRD consecutive writer of that file to hit it: v1.147.1 raised 40,000 -> 43,000 off 3 chars of headroom, v1.149.2 measured 87 and flagged rather than raised, v1.151.2 raised 43,000 -> 45,000 off 38, and origin/dev then spent it down to 15 spare (44,985). The pattern is now the finding: every raise of this file has been consumed within a handful of commits, because it is the behaviour doc of an app that changes every day, and each writer pays a raise-commit toll to add a paragraph. Raised to 50,000 (+11%), a deliberately bigger step than the +7.5% and +4.7% that each lasted ~3 commits — the step size, not the ceiling, is what has been wrong. It is still a cap and still a deliberate act. The archive is untouched at 510,000 (491,139 used) and CLAUDE.md's 82,000 — the only ceiling that is a per-session tax — is untouched at 74,030. RAISED AT v1.165.1, archive only: origin/dev's own recent entries left 509,904 of 510,000 - 96 chars - after the v1.165.2 post-mortem was written, i.e. the 'one entry of headroom, a ceiling-raise commit per entry' condition that v1.147.1 and v1.149.2 each named when raising. 510,000 -> 535,000 (+4.9%), roughly five entries at the observed median. Still a cap, still a deliberate act; the displacement rationale is unaffected (grep target, never auto-loaded) and CLAUDE.md's 82,000 - the only per-session tax - is untouched. RAISED AT v1.173.0, archive only, and the arithmetic names TWO causes so the raise is not credited to one commit that did not cause it. FIRST: origin/dev arrived ALREADY OVER — measured at ada2d1c52, the archive is 536,424 of 535,000 (+1,424), i.e. this gate was red on dev before this branch merged and would have failed the next push whatever it carried. Its own v1.171.0 and v1.172.0 entries (4,328 and 3,987 chars) spent the 3,993 the previous raise left. SECOND: this ship's entry is 6,197 chars — one narrative covering a feature and its owner-feedback follow-up, with a 12-row mutant table — taking the file to 542,767. Raised 535,000 -> 575,000 (+7.5%), leaving ~32,200 after this entry: 6-7 entries at the observed 4-6kB median, rather than the 0.3 the last raise left. This is the SIXTH consecutive raise whose predecessor was consumed within a handful of commits (430,000 -> 445,000 -> 460,000 -> 480,000 -> 510,000 -> 535,000), and every one of those notes concluded the STEP, not the ceiling, was wrong; +7.5% is that lesson applied rather than restated. NOT done with --update, deliberately: that flag sets the ceiling to the EXACT current size (zero headroom — the precise trap these notes describe) and rewrites this _comment, destroying the raise history that is the only evidence for the step-size argument. Still a cap, still a deliberate act. The displacement rationale is unaffected (the archive is a grep target, never auto-loaded, so its size is not a per-session tax) and CLAUDE.md's 82,000 — the only ceiling that IS a per-session tax — is untouched at 78,081. ALSO RAISED AT v1.173.0, docs/Neural.md, and this is the file's own standing instruction being followed rather than deferred: v1.149.2 measured it at 87 chars spare and wrote 'it is left alone here only because this commit does not touch it; the next writer who does will have to raise it first'. This commit DOES touch it — a paragraph for the three bottom layers, plus the see-more deletion and the docking line — and leaves 362 of 50,000. Raised 50,000 -> 54,000 (+8%), which is ~8 paragraphs at the observed size, not one. It remains the file a session actually reads, so the cap stays a cap. RAISED AT v1.189.0, archive only, 600,000 -> 625,000 (+4.2%). Two things worth recording. FIRST, the arithmetic, which is the same one every note above describes: origin/dev arrived at 598,952 of 600,000 - 1,048 chars, i.e. a fifth of one entry at the observed ~5kB median - so the next post-mortem of any size had to raise it, and this one is 7,500 (a policy replacement with a 12-row mutant table and an explicit not-covered section). 625,000 leaves ~18,500 after it: 3-4 entries, not 0.2. SECOND, and this is the new information: the raise from 575,000 to 600,000 happened WITHOUT being written down here, so the step-size argument that every previous note builds - each raise consumed within a handful of commits - lost one of its data points. Not with --update, deliberately, for the reason v1.173.0 gives: --update sets the ceiling to the EXACT current size (zero headroom, the precise trap these notes describe) and rewrites this _comment, destroying the history that is the only evidence for the argument. Still a cap, still a deliberate act; the displacement rationale is unaffected (the archive is a grep target, never auto-loaded, so its size is not a per-session tax) and CLAUDE.md's 82,000 - the only ceiling that IS a per-session tax - is untouched at 80,645, with 1,355 spare after this change's three edited lines. docs/Neural.md is untouched at 53,477: this change is a gate policy, not app behaviour, and its home is the code sites plus this archive. RAISED AT v1.192.3, docs/Neural.md ONLY, 54,000 -> 58,000 (+7.4%), and the arithmetic is the whole argument. MEASURED, not estimated: origin/dev at e5d3fbeb2 is 53,477 of 54,000 - 523 spare. The integration branch merges three branches and one of them, fix-principles (authored v1.190.0, merged here as v1.192.0), writes an 809-char entry into this file: what the deferred Principle body carries, the independent-disclosure preview counts, and the Film-study contract (clips arrive with the body, Shorts first, no study credit, stop on rebuild). 53,477 + 809 = 54,286, i.e. +286 OVER. So the raise is caused by that entry and is credited to it - dev was green, and the other two branches in the batch leave this file untouched. NOTE THE UNIT: the gate counts CHARS. `wc -c` reports 54,818 BYTES for the same file; the 532-char gap is multibyte UTF-8, and reading the byte figure against a char ceiling overstates the overage by roughly twice. WHY NOT TRIMMED, which is what v1.155.3 did in this position: that commit had 857 chars of headroom and an entry that fit inside it. This one does not - fitting 809 into 523 means deleting a third of a paragraph documenting behaviour three curated specs assert, which is exactly what CLAUDE.md section 9 says belongs in the behaviour doc rather than here. WHY 58,000 AND NOT SOME OTHER NUMBER: fix-learning-too hit this identical wall with a 798-char entry and already raised 54,000 -> 58,000 in its own commit. That branch is not in this batch, so its raise does not land - matching its figure rather than inventing a second one is what makes the two resolve trivially when it merges, instead of turning a ceiling into a merge conflict. 58,000 leaves 3,714 after this entry: ~4.6 entries at this one's size, rather than 0.35. THE STEP-SIZE ARGUMENT, which every previous note here builds and which this raise continues: 40,000 -> 43,000 (v1.147.1, +7.5%) -> 45,000 (v1.151.2, +4.7%) -> 50,000 (v1.162.1, +11.1%) -> 54,000 (v1.173.0, +8.0%) -> 58,000 (here, +7.4%). Five raises of this one file, each consumed within a handful of commits, because it is the behaviour doc of an app that changes every day and each writer pays a raise-commit toll to add a paragraph. LABEL CORRECTION, since this file is a grep target: an earlier note above says 'RAISED AT v1.163.0' for the third of those. The commit that actually carries it is v1.162.1 (a584108b2, 'Raise docs/Neural.md again, and the pattern is now the finding'); v1.163.0 (204d06eff) does not touch this file at all. NOT DONE WITH --update, and this time that is a measured fact rather than a preference. It was RUN and reverted, so the behaviour is recorded rather than inferred: unlike the neural ceilings - where check_payload_budget.py's _neural_ceilings() returns min(committed, target) and --update therefore CANNOT raise - this script does ceilings[k] = max(committed, current), so here --update CAN raise. It still cannot do this job, for two independent reasons. (1) It raises to the EXACT current size, 54,286, leaving 0 spare - it takes no target and cannot be asked for 58,000 - which is the zero-headroom trap these notes describe, reached immediately. (2) It REWRITES this _comment with a 200-char generic string, measured: 10,860 chars in, 200 out, destroying the whole raise history that is the only evidence for the step-size argument above. So: hand edit, deliberately. Still a cap, still a deliberate act. UNTOUCHED: CLAUDE.md at 80,645 of 82,000 - the only ceiling that IS a per-session tax, and nothing in this batch adds to it - and docs/Changelog-Archive.md at 606,452 of 625,000.
note: docs/Changelog-Archive.md ceiling 625,000 -> 667,773 on 2026-09-21 (v1.195.11), BY HAND, sized from measurement. Sizes are code points as check_claudemd_budget.py's len() counts them, read from origin/dev history: ab5c74db6 (2026-09-15 11:57) 593,830; e5d3fbeb2 (2026-09-18 11:59) 598,952; 4dc6edfab (2026-09-21 02:17) 610,074; 299b18941 (2026-09-21 09:22) 624,667; 8c2915ec9 (2026-09-21 09:41) 627,666. Growth 33,836 over 5.91 days = 5,730 chars/day; seven days of headroom at that rate = 40,107; ceiling = 627,666 + 40,107 = 667,773. Today's burst alone (+17,592 in 7.4 h, three worker narratives union-merged into the archive) would eat that headroom in ~0.7 days if sustained, which is exactly what a tripwire is for. WHY THIS CEILING IS A BLOAT TRIPWIRE AND NOT A LOAD BUDGET: CLAUDE.md section 0 says the archive is grep'd, never read whole, so its size is not a per-session tax (CLAUDE.md's own ceiling is); section 9 makes it the append-only destination for every commit's narrative, so the checker's advice 'move the narrative to docs/Changelog-Archive.md' is circular for this file. A trip here therefore has two honest answers only: a raise sized from measured growth with the basis written here, or a decision that the growth itself is the problem. NEVER --update for this: measured 2026-09-20, it sets the ceiling to the exact current size with zero headroom and rewrites this file to _comment + ceilings only, dropping this note and truncating _comment from ~10,000 chars to 200. Recompute: for r in ab5c74db6 e5d3fbeb2 4dc6edfab 299b18941 8c2915ec9; do git show $r:docs/Changelog-Archive.md | python3 -c 'import sys; print(len(sys.stdin.read()))'; done
